requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT explicitly set this value to 1.  A server MAY
      choose to omit this setting when it sends a SETTINGS frame, but if
      a server does include a value, it MUST be 0.  A client MUST treat
      receipt of a SETTINGS frame with SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH set to 1 as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a server sends SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit the setting or set its value to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not explicitly set the value to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound server SETTINGS frames can be inspected for omission or the required zero value.

requirements.quote:
A server MUST NOT explicitly set this value to 1.  A server MAY
      choose to omit this setting when it sends a SETTINGS frame, but if
      a server does include a value, it MUST be 0.  A client MUST treat
      receipt of a SETTINGS frame with SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH set to 1 as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a SETTINGS frame whose SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value is 1.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted SETTINGS frame with value 1 can be supplied and the resulting connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (0x03):  This setting indicates the
      maximum number of concurrent streams that the sender will allow.
      This limit is directional: it applies to the number of streams
      that the sender permits the receiver to create.  Initially, there
      is no limit to this value.  It is recommended that this value be
      no smaller than 100, so as to not unnecessarily limit parallelism.
requirements.condition: When enforcing SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS received from a peer.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the limit directionally to streams that the setting sender permits the receiver to create.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can count concurrently created streams in each direction and verify that only the direction governed by the setting is limited.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (0x03):  This setting indicates the
      maximum number of concurrent streams that the sender will allow.
      This limit is directional: it applies to the number of streams
      that the sender permits the receiver to create.  Initially, there
      is no limit to this value.  It is recommended that this value be
      no smaller than 100, so as to not unnecessarily limit parallelism.
requirements.condition: Before SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS has been changed from its initial value.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the setting as having no limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial connection behavior can be tested without advertising this setting and checking whether an implementation imposes a setting-derived numeric limit.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (0x03):  This setting indicates the
      maximum number of concurrent streams that the sender will allow.
      This limit is directional: it applies to the number of streams
      that the sender permits the receiver to create.  Initially, there
      is no limit to this value.  It is recommended that this value be
      no smaller than 100, so as to not unnecessarily limit parallelism.
requirements.condition: When choosing a nonzero SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS value.
requirements.required_behavior: Prefer a value no smaller than 100.
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised numeric value can be compared with 100, although the text expresses a recommendation rather than an absolute requirement.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 for SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS SHOULD NOT be
      treated as special by endpoints.  A zero value does prevent the
      creation of new streams; however, this can also happen for any
      limit that is exhausted with active streams.  Servers SHOULD only
      set a zero value for short durations; if a server does not wish to
      accept requests, closing the connection is more appropriate.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS with value 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle zero as an exhausted concurrent-stream limit, preventing creation of new streams.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not give zero special semantics distinct from an exhausted limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero setting can be injected and attempts to create new streams can be compared with behavior under another exhausted limit.

requirements.quote:
A value of 0 for SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS SHOULD NOT be
      treated as special by endpoints.  A zero value does prevent the
      creation of new streams; however, this can also happen for any
      limit that is exhausted with active streams.  Servers SHOULD only
      set a zero value for short durations; if a server does not wish to
      accept requests, closing the connection is more appropriate.
requirements.condition: When a server advertises SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS as 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the zero value only for a short duration.
requirements.why_checkable: The duration of a zero advertisement is observable, but the chunk provides no objective bound for "short durations".

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE (0x04):  This setting indicates the
      sender's initial window size (in units of octets) for stream-level
      flow control.  The initial value is 2^16-1 (65,535) octets.
requirements.condition: Before SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE has been changed from its initial value.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an initial stream-level flow-control window of 65,535 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial stream flow-control allowance can be measured and compared with 65,535 octets.

requirements.quote:
This setting affects the window size of all streams (see
      Section 6.9.2).
requirements.condition: When SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE is applied.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply its effect to the window size of all streams.
requirements.why_checkable: Window state for every existing and applicable stream can be inspected before and after applying the setting.

requirements.quote:
Values above the maximum flow-control window size of 2^31-1 MUST
      be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE value is greater than 2^31-1.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the value as a connection error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A value above the numeric maximum can be injected and the connection-level error type observed.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE (0x05):  This setting indicates the size of
      the largest frame payload that the sender is willing to receive,
      in units of octets.
requirements.condition: When a peer has advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the setting as the largest frame payload, in octets, that its sender is willing to receive.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated outbound frame payload sizes can be compared with the peer's advertised maximum.

requirements.quote:
The initial value is 2^14 (16,384) octets.  The value advertised
      by an endpoint MUST be between this initial value and the maximum
      allowed frame size (2^24-1 or 16,777,215 octets), inclusive.
      Values outside this range MUST be treated as a connection error
      (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: Before SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE has been changed from its initial value.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 16,384 octets as the initial maximum frame payload size.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial frame-size handling can be tested against the exact 16,384-octet value.

requirements.quote:
The initial value is 2^14 (16,384) octets.  The value advertised
      by an endpoint MUST be between this initial value and the maximum
      allowed frame size (2^24-1 or 16,777,215 octets), inclusive.
      Values outside this range MUST be treated as a connection error
      (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint advertises SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise a value from 16,384 through 16,777,215 octets, inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not advertise a value below 16,384 or above 16,777,215.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded setting value can be checked against the inclusive numeric range.

requirements.quote:
The initial value is 2^14 (16,384) octets.  The value advertised
      by an endpoint MUST be between this initial value and the maximum
      allowed frame size (2^24-1 or 16,777,215 octets), inclusive.
      Values outside this range MUST be treated as a connection error
      (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE below 16,384 or above 16,777,215.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the value as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Out-of-range values can be injected at both boundaries and the connection error type observed.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE (0x06):  This advisory setting informs
      a peer of the maximum field section size that the sender is
      prepared to accept, in units of octets.  The value is based on the
      uncompressed size of field lines, including the length of the name
      and value in units of octets plus an overhead of 32 octets for
      each field line.
requirements.condition: When calculating field section size for SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the uncompressed octet lengths of every field name and value, plus 32 octets of overhead for each field line.
requirements.why_checkable: A known set of field lines has a deterministic size under the stated formula, which can be compared with implementation acceptance behavior.

requirements.quote:
For any given request, a lower limit than what is advertised MAY
      be enforced.  The initial value of this setting is unlimited.
requirements.condition: For an individual request subject to SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation may enforce a lower limit than the advertised value.
requirements.why_checkable: Requests sized below the advertised value can reveal whether a configured lower per-request limit is enforced.

requirements.quote:
For any given request, a lower limit than what is advertised MAY
      be enforced.  The initial value of this setting is unlimited.
requirements.condition: Before SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE has been changed from its initial value.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the setting's initial value as unlimited.
requirements.why_checkable: Initial behavior can be tested without receiving the setting and checked for absence of a setting-derived finite limit.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives a SETTINGS frame with any unknown or
   unsupported identifier MUST ignore that setting.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a SETTINGS entry with an unknown or unsupported identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore that setting.
requirements.why_checkable: An unknown identifier can be injected and the connection and other settings can be checked for unaffected processing.

requirements.quote:
Most values in SETTINGS benefit from or require an understanding of
   when the peer has received and applied the changed parameter values.
   In order to provide such synchronization timepoints, the recipient of
   a SETTINGS frame in which the ACK flag is not set MUST apply the
   updated settings as soon as possible upon receipt.  SETTINGS frames
   are acknowledged in the order in which they are received.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS frame without the ACK flag is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the updated settings as soon as possible upon receipt.
requirements.why_checkable: Setting-dependent behavior can be exercised immediately after frame receipt to detect whether the update was applied.

requirements.quote:
Most values in SETTINGS benefit from or require an understanding of
   when the peer has received and applied the changed parameter values.
   In order to provide such synchronization timepoints, the recipient of
   a SETTINGS frame in which the ACK flag is not set MUST apply the
   updated settings as soon as possible upon receipt.  SETTINGS frames
   are acknowledged in the order in which they are received.
requirements.condition: When multiple SETTINGS frames await acknowledgment.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the SETTINGS frames in the order received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not acknowledge a later SETTINGS frame before an earlier one.
requirements.why_checkable: Multiple SETTINGS frames can be sent in sequence and the corresponding ACK sequence observed.

requirements.quote:
The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they
   appear, with no other frame processing between values.  Unsupported
   settings MUST be ignored.  Once all values have been processed, the
   recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag
   set.  Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the
   sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest
   unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
requirements.condition: When processing multiple values within one SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Process the values in their encoded order.
requirements.why_checkable: Order-dependent repeated or interacting setting values can expose whether wire order was preserved.

requirements.quote:
The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they
   appear, with no other frame processing between values.  Unsupported
   settings MUST be ignored.  Once all values have been processed, the
   recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag
   set.  Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the
   sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest
   unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
requirements.condition: While processing the values in a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Process all of that frame's values atomically with respect to other frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process another frame between SETTINGS values.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation or order-sensitive frame sequences can detect interleaving between values of one SETTINGS frame.

requirements.quote:
The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they
   appear, with no other frame processing between values.  Unsupported
   settings MUST be ignored.  Once all values have been processed, the
   recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag
   set.  Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the
   sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest
   unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
requirements.condition: When an unsupported setting appears among SETTINGS frame values.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the unsupported setting while continuing processing of the frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame mixing supported and unsupported settings can verify that the unsupported entry has no effect and does not prevent supported entries from being processed.

requirements.quote:
The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they
   appear, with no other frame processing between values.  Unsupported
   settings MUST be ignored.  Once all values have been processed, the
   recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag
   set.  Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the
   sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest
   unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
requirements.condition: Once every value in a received non-ACK SETTINGS frame has been processed.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not emit the acknowledgment before all values are processed.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame output and processing events can be ordered to confirm that the ACK follows completion of all values without intervening delay.

requirements.quote:
The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they
   appear, with no other frame processing between values.  Unsupported
   settings MUST be ignored.  Once all values have been processed, the
   recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag
   set.  Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the
   sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest
   unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
requirements.condition: When the sender receives a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the acknowledgment with the oldest unacknowledged SETTINGS frame and regard its values as applied.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not associate the ACK with a newer unacknowledged SETTINGS frame while an older one remains.
requirements.why_checkable: Several outstanding SETTINGS frames with distinguishable effects can verify FIFO acknowledgment association.

requirements.quote:
If the sender of a SETTINGS frame does not receive an acknowledgment
   within a reasonable amount of time, it MAY issue a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type SETTINGS_TIMEOUT.  In setting a timeout, some
   allowance needs to be made for processing delays at the peer; a
   timeout that is solely based on the round-trip time between endpoints
   might result in spurious errors.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS sender does not receive an acknowledgment within its reasonable timeout.
requirements.error_behavior: It may issue a connection error of type SETTINGS_TIMEOUT.
requirements.why_checkable: With a configured timeout, acknowledgment can be withheld and the resulting connection error type observed.

requirements.quote:
If the sender of a SETTINGS frame does not receive an acknowledgment
   within a reasonable amount of time, it MAY issue a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type SETTINGS_TIMEOUT.  In setting a timeout, some
   allowance needs to be made for processing delays at the peer; a
   timeout that is solely based on the round-trip time between endpoints
   might result in spurious errors.
requirements.condition: When selecting the SETTINGS acknowledgment timeout.
requirements.required_behavior: Make some allowance for peer processing delays.
requirements.why_checkable: The timeout calculation can be inspected, but the chunk gives no minimum allowance or precise algorithm.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUSH_PROMISE frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Length as 24 bits and Type as an 8-bit value fixed to 0x05.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame header bit widths and fixed type value can be inspected directly on the wire.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (4),
     PADDED Flag (1),
     END_HEADERS Flag (1),
     Unused Flags (2),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing PUSH_PROMISE flags.
requirements.required_behavior: Use four unused flag bits, followed by one PADDED bit, one END_HEADERS bit, and two unused flag bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The eight-bit flags field layout can be checked bit by bit.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PUSH_PROMISE frame stream identifier field.
requirements.required_behavior: Use one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit Stream Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The 32-bit field can be decoded and checked for the specified partition.

requirements.quote:
[Pad Length (8)],
     Reserved (1),
     Promised Stream ID (31),
     Field Block Fragment (..),
     Padding (..2040),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUSH_PROMISE payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an optional 8-bit Pad Length, a one-bit reserved field, a 31-bit Promised Stream ID, a variable-length Field Block Fragment, and zero through 2040 bits of Padding in that order.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload field order, widths, optionality, and padding bound can be checked against encoded bytes.

requirements.quote:
Pad Length:  An 8-bit field containing the length of the frame
      padding in units of octets.  This field is only present if the
      PADDED flag is set.
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE frame has the PADDED flag set.
requirements.required_behavior: Include an 8-bit Pad Length field containing the padding length in octets.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames with PADDED set can be decoded to verify field presence, width, and agreement with padding length.

requirements.quote:
Pad Length:  An 8-bit field containing the length of the frame
      padding in units of octets.  This field is only present if the
      PADDED flag is set.
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE frame does not have the PADDED flag set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Pad Length field.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames without PADDED can be decoded to verify that payload parsing starts directly with the next field.

requirements.quote:
Promised Stream ID:  An unsigned 31-bit integer that identifies the
      stream that is reserved by the PUSH_PROMISE.  The promised stream
      identifier MUST be a valid choice for the next stream sent by the
      sender (see "new stream identifier" in Section 5.1.1).
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing Promised Stream ID in a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the identifier as an unsigned 31-bit integer identifying the stream reserved by the PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width, unsigned interpretation, and association with the reserved stream can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Promised Stream ID:  An unsigned 31-bit integer that identifies the
      stream that is reserved by the PUSH_PROMISE.  The promised stream
      identifier MUST be a valid choice for the next stream sent by the
      sender (see "new stream identifier" in Section 5.1.1).
requirements.condition: When a sender selects the Promised Stream ID for a PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: Select an identifier that is valid for the sender's next stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised identifier can be compared with the sender's stream-identifier sequence and validity state.

requirements.quote:
Field Block Fragment:  A field block fragment (Section 4.3)
      containing the request control data and a header section.
requirements.condition: When constructing or parsing the Field Block Fragment of a PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a field block fragment containing request control data and a header section.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded field block can be inspected for the specified request control data and header section.

requirements.quote:
Padding:  Padding octets that contain no application semantic value.
      Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.  A receiver is
      not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending a padded PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Set every padding octet to zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send non-zero padding octets.
requirements.why_checkable: Every transmitted padding octet can be inspected directly for a zero value.

requirements.quote:
Padding:  Padding octets that contain no application semantic value.
      Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.  A receiver is
      not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a receiver detects non-zero padding in a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.error_behavior: It may treat the non-zero padding as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame containing non-zero padding can be injected and the receiver's permitted connection-error behavior observed.
